4.1.title: Context and external issues
4.1.author: Omnisciente
4.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
4.1.plain: The ISMS needs to reflect the business conditions in which it operates, including whether climate change is relevant to that context.
4.1.start: Compare recorded context decisions with the organization's actual strategy, operations and relevant dependencies.
4.1.evidence: Recorded context analysis and climate relevance decision; a dedicated register is one possible format.
4.1.ask: Consult business leadership and the ISMS owner. Which business or climate-related conditions were considered, and what effect did they have on security priorities?
4.1.gaps: Context analysis is generic or climate relevance has no considered decision.
review: Compare recorded context decisions with the organization's actual strategy, operations and relevant dependencies.
Consult business leadership and the ISMS owner. Which business or climate-related conditions were considered, and what effect did they have on security priorities?
evidence_examples: Recorded context analysis and climate relevance decision; a dedicated register is one possible format.
Recorded context workshop decisions explaining relevant issues and climate relevance.
outcome: Context decisions explain relevant conditions and climate relevance.

4.2.title: Stakeholder obligations
4.2.author: Omnisciente
4.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
4.2.plain: Understand whose needs and obligations matter to the ISMS and which of those expectations it addresses, including relevant climate concerns.
4.2.start: Trace relevant interested-party expectations into the recorded requirements the ISMS addresses.
4.2.evidence: Recorded interested-party analysis and relevant requirements with responsibility for addressing them; a register is one possible format.
4.2.ask: Consult the ISMS owner and owners of relevant stakeholder relationships. Who decides which stakeholder expectations the ISMS must address?
4.2.gaps: Interested parties are listed without relevant requirements or accountable owners.
review: Trace relevant interested-party expectations into the recorded requirements the ISMS addresses.
Consult the ISMS owner and owners of relevant stakeholder relationships. Who decides which stakeholder expectations the ISMS must address?
evidence_examples: Recorded interested-party analysis and relevant requirements with responsibility for addressing them; a register is one possible format.
A stakeholder analysis in Client Profile with relevant requirements and responsible owners.
outcome: Stakeholder requirements have owners and a stated ISMS response.

4.3.title: ISMS boundaries
4.3.author: Omnisciente
4.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
4.3.plain: Make the ISMS boundary understandable: the locations, services, interfaces and dependencies that the management system covers.
4.3.start: Compare the documented scope with actual operations, locations, information flows and relevant external interfaces.
4.3.evidence: Documented ISMS scope with understandable boundaries and dependencies; a diagram can support the explanation.
4.3.ask: Consult the ISMS owner and owners of in-scope operations. If the scope has boundary exclusions, how are their dependencies and justification understood?
4.3.gaps: Scope omits a critical interface or claims coverage beyond actual operations.
review: Compare the documented scope with actual operations, locations, information flows and relevant external interfaces.
Consult the ISMS owner and owners of in-scope operations. If the scope has boundary exclusions, how are their dependencies and justification understood?
evidence_examples: Documented ISMS scope with understandable boundaries and dependencies; a diagram can support the explanation.
A controlled scope description with service and dependency boundaries; a diagram is optional.
outcome: The documented scope matches real locations, services and interfaces.

4.4.title: ISMS processes
4.4.author: Omnisciente
4.4.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
4.4.plain: The ISMS is a set of connected operating processes, not just a collection of security documents.
4.4.start: Follow one risk through assessment, treatment, review and improvement processes.
4.4.evidence: An operating description of ISMS processes, their interactions and accountable ownership; a process map is one possible format.
4.4.ask: Consult the ISMS owner and relevant process owners. How do the ISMS processes exchange decisions and records?
4.4.gaps: Processes exist as isolated documents with no working handoffs.
review: Follow one risk through assessment, treatment, review and improvement processes.
Consult the ISMS owner and relevant process owners. How do the ISMS processes exchange decisions and records?
evidence_examples: An operating description of ISMS processes, their interactions and accountable ownership; a process map is one possible format.
An ISMS operating description with process owners and evidence of actual handoffs.
outcome: ISMS process handoffs work across risk, treatment and oversight.

5.1.title: Leadership accountability
5.1.author: Omnisciente
5.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
5.1.plain: Leadership support should be visible in decisions, resources and the way information security is integrated into business activity.
5.1.start: Inspect a recent leadership decision that allocated resources or resolved a security issue.
5.1.ask: Consult executive leadership and the ISMS owner. What leadership decisions demonstrate that security considerations influence business priorities?
5.1.gaps: A sponsor is named but decisions and resource support cannot be demonstrated.
review: Inspect a recent leadership decision that allocated resources or resolved a security issue.
Consult executive leadership and the ISMS owner. What leadership decisions demonstrate that security considerations influence business priorities?
evidence_examples: Leadership decisions and resource commitments.
Meeting decisions or approved resource requests showing leadership involvement.
outcome: Leadership decisions demonstrate resources and security integration.

5.2.title: Security policy direction
5.2.author: Omnisciente
5.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
5.2.plain: Security policy communicates management direction and provides a basis for objectives; people need to understand the policy relevant to their work.
5.2.start: Check the approved security policy against objectives and workforce communication.
5.2.evidence: Approved policy, communication record and acknowledgements.
5.2.ask: Consult the policy approver and ISMS owner. How does policy direction influence actual security objectives?
5.2.gaps: Policy approval is stale or affected people cannot locate the current policy.
review: Check the approved security policy against objectives and workforce communication.
Consult the policy approver and ISMS owner. How does policy direction influence actual security objectives?
evidence_examples: Approved policy, communication record and acknowledgements.
Controlled policy approval and evidence that affected people received the current direction.
outcome: Policy direction supports objectives and reaches its intended audience.

5.3.title: Accountable ISMS roles
5.3.author: Omnisciente
5.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
5.3.plain: People need clear responsibility for operating the ISMS and reporting its performance and conformity.
5.3.start: Trace ISMS operation and performance reporting to named accountable roles.
5.3.evidence: Communicated role assignments or role descriptions covering ISMS operation and reporting.
5.3.ask: Consult leadership and people assigned ISMS operation or reporting duties. Who reports ISMS performance and who has authority to resolve an ownership dispute?
5.3.gaps: Responsibilities overlap or reporting accountability is absent.
review: Trace ISMS operation and performance reporting to named accountable roles.
Consult leadership and people assigned ISMS operation or reporting duties. Who reports ISMS performance and who has authority to resolve an ownership dispute?
evidence_examples: Communicated role assignments or role descriptions covering ISMS operation and reporting.
Role descriptions or communicated assignments showing operation and reporting accountability.
outcome: ISMS operation and reporting have communicated accountable roles.

6.1.1.title: Planning risks and opportunities
6.1.1.author: Omnisciente
6.1.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
6.1.1.plain: ISMS planning should address relevant risks and opportunities and explain how the chosen actions will be evaluated.
6.1.1.start: Compare planning actions with context issues, stakeholder needs and identified opportunities.
6.1.1.ask: Consult the ISMS planner and relevant risk or process owners. How will you determine whether each planning action achieved its purpose?
6.1.1.gaps: Planning records list risks but omit opportunities or evaluation of chosen actions.
review: Compare planning actions with context issues, stakeholder needs and identified opportunities.
Consult the ISMS planner and relevant risk or process owners. How will you determine whether each planning action achieved its purpose?
evidence_examples: Planning decisions and evaluated actions.
Planning minutes linking risks and opportunities to actions and evaluation methods.
outcome: Planning actions address relevant risks and opportunities with evaluation methods.

6.1.2.title: Risk assessment method
6.1.2.author: Omnisciente
6.1.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
6.1.2.plain: A repeatable risk assessment approach makes criteria, ownership and evaluation consistent enough to support meaningful decisions.
6.1.2.start: Reperform a sample risk assessment using the documented criteria.
6.1.2.ask: Consult the risk-method owner and assessors. Would two assessors reach comparable decisions using the same criteria?
6.1.2.gaps: Likelihood, impact, acceptance criteria or risk ownership are undefined.
review: Reperform a sample risk assessment using the documented criteria.
Consult the risk-method owner and assessors. Would two assessors reach comparable decisions using the same criteria?
evidence_examples: Risk methodology and representative assessments.
A documented assessment procedure with criteria and completed comparable samples.
outcome: Risk assessment criteria support consistent and repeatable decisions.

6.1.3.title: Treatment decisions and SoA
6.1.3.author: Omnisciente
6.1.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
6.1.3.plain: Risk treatment connects selected controls, owner decisions and the Statement of Applicability. Necessary controls are not limited to the Annex A reference set.
6.1.3.start: Trace a selected risk through treatment options, necessary controls and SoA decisions.
6.1.3.evidence: Risk treatment plan, residual-risk acceptance and SoA decisions.
6.1.3.ask: Consult risk owners and the person coordinating risk treatment and the SoA. How did comparison with Annex A and other necessary controls support the completeness of treatment decisions?
6.1.3.gaps: SoA exclusions lack justification or residual risk decisions lack owner approval.
review: Trace a selected risk through treatment options, necessary controls and SoA decisions.
Consult risk owners and the person coordinating risk treatment and the SoA. How did comparison with Annex A and other necessary controls support the completeness of treatment decisions?
evidence_examples: Risk treatment plan, residual-risk acceptance and SoA decisions.
Linked risk, treatment and SoA records with owner decisions and custom-control consideration.
outcome: Treatments and SoA decisions account for necessary controls and owner acceptance.

6.2.title: Measurable security objectives
6.2.author: Omnisciente
6.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
6.2.plain: Information security objectives need an accountable plan and measures that show whether progress is being made.
6.2.start: Inspect one objective from measurable target through measurement results and its delivery plan.
6.2.ask: Consult objective owners and the people responsible for measurement. What result would show this objective succeeded within its timeframe?
6.2.gaps: Objectives are one-time tasks or have no measure, owner or reporting period.
review: Inspect one objective from measurable target through measurement results and its delivery plan.
Consult objective owners and the people responsible for measurement. What result would show this objective succeeded within its timeframe?
evidence_examples: Objectives register and measurement results.
Objective records with target, owner, measurement method, timeframe and measured results.
outcome: Objective results can be compared with accountable measurable targets.

6.3.title: Planned ISMS changes
6.3.author: Omnisciente
6.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
6.3.plain: Changes to the ISMS should be planned so their impact and implementation are understood rather than accidental.
6.3.start: Sample a change to ISMS scope, processes or ownership and inspect its plan.
6.3.evidence: Change proposal, impact analysis and implementation record.
6.3.ask: Consult the ISMS change owner and affected process owners. What dependencies and resource needs were considered before this ISMS change?
6.3.gaps: ISMS changes are implemented without assessing their effects.
review: Sample a change to ISMS scope, processes or ownership and inspect its plan.
Consult the ISMS change owner and affected process owners. What dependencies and resource needs were considered before this ISMS change?
evidence_examples: Change proposal, impact analysis and implementation record.
A planned ISMS change record describing effects, resources and implementation responsibility.
outcome: ISMS changes have understood impacts and planned implementation.

7.1.title: ISMS resources
7.1.author: Omnisciente
7.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.1.plain: The management system needs adequate resources, and identified resource gaps need an accountable response.
7.1.start: Compare ISMS workload and skills needs with approved resource allocation.
7.1.evidence: Resource plan and staffing or budget decisions.
7.1.ask: Consult leadership and owners of resource allocation. Which resource constraint could prevent a planned ISMS activity?
7.1.gaps: Funding or staffing gaps are recognized but have no accountable response.
review: Compare ISMS workload and skills needs with approved resource allocation.
Consult leadership and owners of resource allocation. Which resource constraint could prevent a planned ISMS activity?
evidence_examples: Resource plan and staffing or budget decisions.
A resource decision or capacity review resolving identified ISMS needs.
outcome: ISMS resource needs are met or assigned an accountable resolution.

7.2.title: Role competence
7.2.author: Omnisciente
7.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.2.plain: People carrying out relevant responsibilities need demonstrable competence, not simply an assigned job title.
7.2.start: Sample people performing relevant ISMS responsibilities, such as risk assessment, audit or incident handling.
7.2.evidence: Competence matrix and training or experience records.
7.2.ask: Consult line managers and the person responsible for competence assurance. How was competence established and how was any learning action evaluated?
7.2.gaps: Training attendance is used as the sole proof of competence.
review: Sample people performing relevant ISMS responsibilities, such as risk assessment, audit or incident handling.
Consult line managers and the person responsible for competence assurance. How was competence established and how was any learning action evaluated?
evidence_examples: Competence matrix and training or experience records.
Experience or qualification records plus evaluation of competence for the assigned duties.
outcome: Relevant responsibilities are supported by demonstrable competence.

7.3.title: Workforce awareness
7.3.author: Omnisciente
7.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.3.plain: People should understand the security policy, their contribution and the consequences of departing from ISMS expectations.
7.3.start: Ask a workforce member to explain reporting routes and security responsibilities.
7.3.ask: Consult workforce members and the awareness coordinator. What happens when an employee departs from an ISMS expectation?
7.3.gaps: Awareness completion records exist but people cannot explain their contribution.
review: Ask a workforce member to explain reporting routes and security responsibilities.
Consult workforce members and the awareness coordinator. What happens when an employee departs from an ISMS expectation?
evidence_examples: Awareness materials and completion evidence.
Interview observations or exercises showing awareness of responsibilities and reporting routes.
outcome: Workforce members can explain their security contribution and consequences.

7.4.title: ISMS communications
7.4.author: Omnisciente
7.4.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.4.plain: ISMS communication should have a clear purpose, audience, owner and timing so important information reaches the right people.
7.4.start: Inspect communication arrangements for relevant ISMS activities, such as policy updates, performance reporting or incident escalation.
7.4.ask: Consult the ISMS communication owner and intended recipients. Who receives each communication, through which route and at what trigger?
7.4.gaps: Communications lack audience, responsibility or timing.
review: Inspect communication arrangements for relevant ISMS activities, such as policy updates, performance reporting or incident escalation.
Consult the ISMS communication owner and intended recipients. Who receives each communication, through which route and at what trigger?
evidence_examples: Communication plan and delivery evidence.
A communication plan or process description identifying audience, timing and responsibility.
outcome: Communication routes specify purpose, audience, responsibility and timing.

7.5.1.title: Required records
7.5.1.author: Omnisciente
7.5.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.5.1.plain: Operating and demonstrating this ISMS depends on appropriate documentation with clear controlled locations.
7.5.1.start: Locate the records needed to operate and demonstrate the in-scope ISMS.
7.5.1.ask: Consult the ISMS owner and owners of necessary operating records. Which records are needed for your processes beyond the standard's references?
7.5.1.gaps: Required records are absent or scattered without controlled locations.
review: Locate the records needed to operate and demonstrate the in-scope ISMS.
Consult the ISMS owner and owners of necessary operating records. Which records are needed for your processes beyond the standard's references?
evidence_examples: Document register and current records.
Controlled records distributed across existing modules with clear ownership and retrieval paths.
outcome: Necessary operating and demonstration records have controlled locations.

7.5.2.title: Document creation and revision
7.5.2.author: Omnisciente
7.5.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.5.2.plain: New and changed documents need appropriate identification, review and approval before people rely on them.
7.5.2.start: Sample a revised procedure and inspect identification, review and approval.
7.5.2.ask: Consult document authors and assigned reviewers or approvers. How can a reader tell whether a new version is approved for use?
7.5.2.gaps: Changes are published with no review or version identity.
review: Sample a revised procedure and inspect identification, review and approval.
Consult document authors and assigned reviewers or approvers. How can a reader tell whether a new version is approved for use?
evidence_examples: Document versions and review approvals.
Document history or workflow records demonstrating identification, review and approval.
outcome: New or revised documents are identifiable, reviewed and approved.

7.5.3.title: Document protection and availability
7.5.3.author: Omnisciente
7.5.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
7.5.3.plain: Documentation needs controlled access, distribution, retention and revision handling, including relevant external documents.
7.5.3.start: Test retrieval and access to a current document and its superseded version.
7.5.3.evidence: Access controls, retention schedule and revision history.
7.5.3.ask: Consult document owners and people administering controlled repositories. How do you protect external documents and prevent obsolete instructions being used?
7.5.3.gaps: Readers use uncontrolled copies or retention and disposal are undefined.
review: Test retrieval and access to a current document and its superseded version.
Consult document owners and people administering controlled repositories. How do you protect external documents and prevent obsolete instructions being used?
evidence_examples: Access controls, retention schedule and revision history.
Repository permissions and revision history demonstrating protection and current-version access.
outcome: Current and superseded documentation has controlled access and handling.

8.1.title: Controlled operational processes
8.1.author: Omnisciente
8.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
8.1.plain: Planned ISMS activities and relevant externally provided processes need to be carried out under understood operating controls.
8.1.start: Sample a planned operational activity and, where relevant, an externally provided process.
8.1.ask: Consult operational process owners. Which operating criteria show the process ran as planned? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
8.1.gaps: Execution lacks defined criteria or supplier-controlled activities have no oversight.
review: Sample a planned operational activity and, where relevant, an externally provided process.
Consult operational process owners. Which operating criteria show the process ran as planned? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
evidence_examples: Operating procedures and execution records.
Operating records or sampled supplier oversight showing defined criteria were followed.
outcome: Operational and externally provided processes meet defined operating criteria.

8.2.title: Risk assessment execution
8.2.author: Omnisciente
8.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
8.2.plain: Risk assessment remains an operating activity, including planned reassessment and reassessment following significant changes.
8.2.start: Compare completed assessments with the risk review plan and significant change history.
8.2.evidence: Dated risk assessments and change-triggered reassessments.
8.2.ask: Consult risk assessors and affected risk owners. Which change would trigger reassessment outside the planned schedule?
8.2.gaps: Risk assessment records were not refreshed after a material change.
review: Compare completed assessments with the risk review plan and significant change history.
Consult risk assessors and affected risk owners. Which change would trigger reassessment outside the planned schedule?
evidence_examples: Dated risk assessments and change-triggered reassessments.
Dated assessments linked to the planned reassessment cycle or significant-change trigger.
outcome: Risk reassessment reflects planned activity and significant change.

8.3.title: Treatment execution
8.3.author: Omnisciente
8.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
8.3.plain: Agreed risk treatment needs to be implemented; a treatment plan without execution evidence leaves that work unproven.
8.3.start: Follow a treatment plan to deployed safeguards, test evidence and retained results.
8.3.ask: Consult treatment owners and people implementing the selected safeguards. What demonstrates that a completed treatment actually changed the exposure? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
8.3.gaps: Treatments are marked complete without implementation evidence.
review: Follow a treatment plan to deployed safeguards, test evidence and retained results.

Consult treatment owners and people implementing the selected safeguards. What demonstrates that a completed treatment actually changed the exposure? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
evidence_examples: Treatment Actions and risk-owner decisions.
Treatment records linked to actual implementation checks and retained results.
outcome: Agreed treatments have retained implementation results.

9.1.title: Performance measurement
9.1.author: Omnisciente
9.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
9.1.plain: Useful performance evaluation connects defined measures, responsibilities and timing to retained results and conclusions.
9.1.start: Recalculate one performance measure from its source data and inspect the conclusion.
9.1.evidence: Metric definitions, results and evaluation records.
9.1.ask: Consult measurement owners and people analyzing or evaluating ISMS performance. Who measures, analyzes and evaluates results, and when?
9.1.gaps: Metrics have no method or collected results are never evaluated.
review: Recalculate one performance measure from its source data and inspect the conclusion.
Consult measurement owners and people analyzing or evaluating ISMS performance. Who measures, analyzes and evaluates results, and when?
evidence_examples: Metric definitions, results and evaluation records.
A measurement record with method, source data, analysis and conclusions.
outcome: Performance results support analysis and evaluation of ISMS effectiveness.

9.2.1.title: ISMS audit coverage
9.2.1.author: Omnisciente
9.2.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
9.2.1.plain: Internal audit evaluates the ISMS against its relevant criteria rather than merely collecting evidence that activities occurred.
9.2.1.start: Compare an audit's criteria and tests with ISMS requirements and the organization's own rules.
9.2.1.evidence: Internal audit scope, criteria and reports.
9.2.1.ask: Consult the internal auditor and owners of the audited processes. Did the audit evaluate implementation and effectiveness as well as document presence?
9.2.1.gaps: Audit tests are a document inventory rather than evaluation against criteria.
review: Compare an audit's criteria and tests with ISMS requirements and the organization's own rules.
Consult the internal auditor and owners of the audited processes. Did the audit evaluate implementation and effectiveness as well as document presence?
evidence_examples: Internal audit scope, criteria and reports.
An audit report with relevant criteria, performed tests and supported conclusions.
outcome: Audit tests evaluate the ISMS against its relevant criteria.

9.2.2.title: Internal audit programme
9.2.2.author: Omnisciente
9.2.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
9.2.2.plain: The audit programme needs deliberate planning, impartiality, reporting and follow-up so its results support reliable oversight.
9.2.2.start: Review programme coverage, auditor impartiality and follow-up for completed audits.
9.2.2.evidence: Audit programme, auditor independence and reports.
9.2.2.ask: Consult the audit programme owner and assigned auditors. How do process importance and earlier audit results affect the programme?
9.2.2.gaps: Coverage is incomplete or an auditor assesses their own work without safeguards.
review: Review programme coverage, auditor impartiality and follow-up for completed audits.
Consult the audit programme owner and assigned auditors. How do process importance and earlier audit results affect the programme?
evidence_examples: Audit programme, auditor independence and reports.
An audit programme with coverage decisions, impartial assignments and reporting follow-up.
outcome: The audit programme provides planned coverage, impartiality and follow-up.

9.3.1.title: Management review operation
9.3.1.author: Omnisciente
9.3.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
9.3.1.plain: Management review is leadership's evaluation of ISMS suitability and effectiveness, distinct from internal audit.
9.3.1.start: Inspect a completed leadership review and its schedule or change triggers.
9.3.1.evidence: Dated management review minutes and attendance.
9.3.1.ask: Consult the management-review chair and ISMS owner. How did management decide the ISMS remains suitable and effective?
9.3.1.gaps: Management review is a status meeting with no ISMS evaluation.
review: Inspect a completed leadership review and its schedule or change triggers.
Consult the management-review chair and ISMS owner. How did management decide the ISMS remains suitable and effective?
evidence_examples: Dated management review minutes and attendance.
A retained management-review record showing leadership evaluation and timing.
outcome: Leadership review evaluates ISMS suitability and effectiveness.

9.3.2.title: Management review inputs
9.3.2.author: Omnisciente
9.3.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
9.3.2.plain: Management review needs relevant inputs, including performance, changes, feedback, risk and follow-up on earlier decisions.
9.3.2.start: Check the review input pack against performance, feedback, risk and previous decisions.
9.3.2.evidence: Management review pack linked to authoritative records.
9.3.2.ask: Consult the review coordinator and owners of relevant input records. Which changed conditions or stakeholder feedback influenced the review?
9.3.2.gaps: Inputs omit unresolved previous actions, risk changes or audit results.
review: Check the review input pack against performance, feedback, risk and previous decisions.
Consult the review coordinator and owners of relevant input records. Which changed conditions or stakeholder feedback influenced the review?
evidence_examples: Management review pack linked to authoritative records.
A structured input pack or linked source records considered during management review.
outcome: Review inputs reflect changes, performance, feedback, risk and prior decisions.

9.3.3.title: Management review decisions
9.3.3.author: Omnisciente
9.3.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
9.3.3.plain: Management review should lead to recorded improvement or change decisions with accountable follow-through.
9.3.3.start: Trace review decisions into improvements, ISMS changes and assigned actions.
9.3.3.evidence: Approved minutes and linked Action Items.
9.3.3.ask: Consult management-review decision makers and assigned action owners. Where are management decisions and their follow-through retained?
9.3.3.gaps: Minutes contain discussion but no recorded decision or accountable action.
review: Trace review decisions into improvements, ISMS changes and assigned actions.
Consult management-review decision makers and assigned action owners. Where are management decisions and their follow-through retained?
evidence_examples: Approved minutes and linked Action Items.
Review decisions linked to assigned improvements or ISMS change records.
outcome: Management decisions lead to accountable improvements or ISMS changes.

10.1.title: Ongoing ISMS improvement
10.1.author: Omnisciente
10.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
10.1.plain: Improvement means making changes and evaluating their effectiveness, not just identifying opportunities.
10.1.start: Trace an improvement from identified opportunity to implemented change and evaluation.
10.1.ask: Consult the ISMS owner and improvement owners. How do you know the change improved the ISMS rather than only adding work?
10.1.gaps: Improvement opportunities accumulate without implementation or evaluation.
review: Trace an improvement from identified opportunity to implemented change and evaluation.
Consult the ISMS owner and improvement owners. How do you know the change improved the ISMS rather than only adding work?
evidence_examples: Improvement decisions and before/after evidence.
An improvement record showing implementation and subsequent evaluation.
outcome: Implemented improvements are evaluated for their intended effect.

10.2.title: Nonconformity correction
10.2.author: Omnisciente
10.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
10.2.plain: Corrective action connects a deficiency to its cause, remediation and effectiveness validation; completing a task alone does not demonstrate resolution.
10.2.start: Inspect a nonconformity from containment and cause analysis through effectiveness verification.
10.2.evidence: Finding history, remediation and validation results.
10.2.ask: Consult the finding owner and person verifying corrective-action effectiveness. What prevents this issue recurring or appearing elsewhere?
10.2.gaps: Action closure substitutes for cause analysis or effectiveness verification.
review: Inspect a nonconformity from containment and cause analysis through effectiveness verification.
Consult the finding owner and person verifying corrective-action effectiveness. What prevents this issue recurring or appearing elsewhere?
evidence_examples: Finding history, remediation and validation results.
A finding record showing cause analysis, correction and effectiveness verification.
outcome: Nonconformity handling addresses cause, recurrence and effectiveness.

A.5.1.title: Security policy governance
A.5.1.author: Omnisciente
A.5.1.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.1.plain: Keep security policy aligned with management direction and make it usable by the people expected to follow it.
A.5.1.start: Sample policy approval, communication and a review prompted by change.
A.5.1.evidence: Approved policies, ownership, communication and review records.
A.5.1.ask: Consult policy owners, approvers and affected workforce representatives. Which business change last led you to revise a security policy?
A.5.1.gaps: Policies have owners but no evidence of current direction or communication.
review: Sample policy approval, communication and a review prompted by change.
Consult policy owners, approvers and affected workforce representatives. Which business change last led you to revise a security policy?
evidence_examples: Approved policies, ownership, communication and review records.
Controlled policy history and records of communication appropriate to affected people.
outcome: Security policies express current direction and reach affected people.

A.5.2.title: Security role allocation
A.5.2.author: Omnisciente
A.5.2.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.2.plain: Assign security responsibilities so important decisions and activities have accountable owners.
A.5.2.start: Match key security activities to communicated role assignments.
A.5.2.evidence: Communicated role descriptions or assignments with security responsibilities; a responsibility matrix is an optional supporting format.
A.5.2.ask: Consult security activity owners and the leadership assigning responsibilities. Who owns each security decision when the usual owner is unavailable?
A.5.2.gaps: Ownership is unclear at handoffs or assignments are not communicated.
review: Match key security activities to communicated role assignments.
Consult security activity owners and the leadership assigning responsibilities. Who owns each security decision when the usual owner is unavailable?
evidence_examples: Communicated role descriptions or assignments with security responsibilities; a responsibility matrix is an optional supporting format.
Role descriptions or service ownership records with communicated security duties.
outcome: Security activities and decisions have communicated accountable owners.

A.5.3.title: Separation of conflicting duties
A.5.3.author: Omnisciente
A.5.3.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.3.plain: Separate duties that could allow one person to misuse a process without an appropriate check.
A.5.3.start: Inspect a high-impact transaction for incompatible permissions and approvals.
A.5.3.evidence: Role design, access assignments, approval paths and compensating review records.
A.5.3.ask: Consult owners of sensitive processes and access-approval responsibilities. Can one person request, approve and execute this sensitive operation?
A.5.3.gaps: Conflicting duties remain combined without an evaluated compensating check.
review: Inspect a high-impact transaction for incompatible permissions and approvals.
Consult owners of sensitive processes and access-approval responsibilities. Can one person request, approve and execute this sensitive operation?
evidence_examples: Role design, access assignments, approval paths and compensating review records.
Sample transactions showing separate approvals or an evaluated compensating review.
outcome: Conflicting duties are separated or supported by evaluated compensating checks.

A.5.4.title: Management security expectations
A.5.4.author: Omnisciente
A.5.4.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.4.plain: Management should make security expectations clear and support their application in day-to-day work.
A.5.4.start: Sample how managers communicate and follow up on team security expectations.
A.5.4.evidence: Management communications, team responsibilities and follow-up records.
A.5.4.ask: Consult line managers and affected team members. How does a manager respond when a team repeatedly ignores a security rule?
A.5.4.gaps: Expectations are delegated to IT with no management follow-up.
review: Sample how managers communicate and follow up on team security expectations.
Consult line managers and affected team members. How does a manager respond when a team repeatedly ignores a security rule?
evidence_examples: Management communications, team responsibilities and follow-up records.
Team meeting decisions or manager follow-up records showing expectations in practice.
outcome: Managers demonstrate follow-up on workforce security expectations.

A.5.5.title: Authority liaison
A.5.5.author: Omnisciente
A.5.5.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.5.plain: Maintain appropriate relationships and contact routes with relevant authorities.
A.5.5.start: Check current authority contact routes and the owner of liaison activities.
A.5.5.evidence: Authority contact list, assigned liaison responsibilities and relevant correspondence.
A.5.5.ask: Consult the authority liaison and incident escalation owner. Who contacts the relevant authority during an urgent security matter?
A.5.5.gaps: Authority contacts are stale or no liaison owner is designated.
review: Check current authority contact routes and the owner of liaison activities.
Consult the authority liaison and incident escalation owner. Who contacts the relevant authority during an urgent security matter?
evidence_examples: Authority contact list, assigned liaison responsibilities and relevant correspondence.
A tested escalation contact route with assigned authority liaison responsibilities.
outcome: Relevant authority liaison routes are current and assigned.

A.5.6.title: Security community liaison
A.5.6.author: Omnisciente
A.5.6.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.6.plain: Use relevant security communities and professional contacts to stay informed and obtain appropriate support.
A.5.6.start: Inspect a useful security-community update and resulting internal action.
A.5.6.evidence: Participation records, information received and examples of resulting action.
A.5.6.ask: Consult the security-community liaison and recipients of relevant updates. Which professional source recently changed your security practice?
A.5.6.gaps: Membership exists without relevant information reaching decision makers.
review: Inspect a useful security-community update and resulting internal action.
Consult the security-community liaison and recipients of relevant updates. Which professional source recently changed your security practice?
evidence_examples: Participation records, information received and examples of resulting action.
Security-community updates linked to internal assessments or resulting decisions.
outcome: Useful security-community information reaches internal decision makers.

A.5.7.title: Threat-informed decisions
A.5.7.author: Omnisciente
A.5.7.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.7.plain: Use relevant threat information to inform security decisions rather than collecting intelligence without a purpose.
A.5.7.start: Follow one threat advisory through relevance analysis into a risk or operational decision.
A.5.7.evidence: Threat sources, analysis notes and linked risk or operational decisions.
A.5.7.ask: Consult the threat-analysis owner and relevant risk or operational decision makers. How do you distinguish actionable threats from irrelevant intelligence?
A.5.7.gaps: Feeds are collected without analysis or action ownership.
review: Follow one threat advisory through relevance analysis into a risk or operational decision.
Consult the threat-analysis owner and relevant risk or operational decision makers. How do you distinguish actionable threats from irrelevant intelligence?
evidence_examples: Threat sources, analysis notes and linked risk or operational decisions.
An advisory assessment linked to a risk update, change request or reasoned no-action decision.
outcome: Threat information supports documented risk or operational decisions.

A.5.8.title: Security in projects
A.5.8.author: Omnisciente
A.5.8.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.8.plain: Include security needs in projects while decisions can still influence design and delivery.
A.5.8.start: Sample a project from security requirements to design review and acceptance.
A.5.8.evidence: Project security requirements, review gates and accepted exceptions.
A.5.8.ask: Consult the project owner and people responsible for security requirements. At which project gate can security concerns still alter delivery?
A.5.8.gaps: Security review occurs only after project decisions become difficult to change.
review: Sample a project from security requirements to design review and acceptance.
Consult the project owner and people responsible for security requirements. At which project gate can security concerns still alter delivery?
evidence_examples: Project security requirements, review gates and accepted exceptions.
Project records showing security requirements and review before key delivery decisions.
outcome: Project security decisions occur while design and delivery can still change.

A.5.9.title: Asset and information inventory
A.5.9.author: Omnisciente
A.5.9.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.9.plain: Know what information and related assets exist and who is responsible for managing them.
A.5.9.start: Reconcile a sample asset or data set with its recorded owner and location.
A.5.9.evidence: Asset/data inventories, assigned owners and reconciliation records.
A.5.9.ask: Consult information or asset owners and inventory maintainers. How are unmanaged assets discovered and assigned an owner?
A.5.9.gaps: Inventory coverage omits relevant information, assets or accountable owners.
review: Reconcile a sample asset or data set with its recorded owner and location.
Consult information or asset owners and inventory maintainers. How are unmanaged assets discovered and assigned an owner?
evidence_examples: Asset/data inventories, assigned owners and reconciliation records.
Inventory exports or owner-confirmed records reconciled to actual information and assets.
outcome: Information and asset records identify owners and actual coverage.

A.5.10.title: Acceptable-use rules
A.5.10.author: Omnisciente
A.5.10.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.10.plain: Define acceptable ways to use information and assets so users understand the boundaries.
A.5.10.start: Compare acceptable-use rules with workforce practice and acknowledgements.
A.5.10.ask: Consult the acceptable-use owner and representative users. What does a user do when business work requires an exception?
A.5.10.gaps: Rules are inaccessible or exceptions are handled informally.
review: Compare acceptable-use rules with workforce practice and acknowledgements.
Consult the acceptable-use owner and representative users. What does a user do when business work requires an exception?
evidence_examples: Acceptable-use rules, communications and acknowledgements.
Published use rules with workforce communication and approved exception records.
outcome: Users understand acceptable-use boundaries and exception routes.

A.5.11.title: Asset return
A.5.11.author: Omnisciente
A.5.11.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.11.plain: Recover organizational assets when a person or relationship no longer needs them.
A.5.11.start: Trace a departing person's assigned assets to recorded return or resolution.
A.5.11.evidence: Asset assignment lists, departure checklists and return records.
A.5.11.ask: Consult asset custodians and people coordinating relationship departures. How do you resolve equipment that is not returned?
A.5.11.gaps: Departure closes while asset return remains unverified.
review: Trace a departing person's assigned assets to recorded return or resolution.
Consult asset custodians and people coordinating relationship departures. How do you resolve equipment that is not returned?
evidence_examples: Asset assignment lists, departure checklists and return records.
Asset custody records linked to return, transfer or explicitly resolved outstanding items.
outcome: Departing relationships leave assets returned or explicitly resolved.

A.5.12.title: Information classification
A.5.12.author: Omnisciente
A.5.12.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.12.plain: Classify information according to its protection needs and business context.
A.5.12.start: Sample data sets and compare classifications with impact and handling needs.
A.5.12.evidence: Classification scheme, data inventory and owner decisions.
A.5.12.ask: Consult information owners and the classification scheme owner. Who decides classification when information changes purpose or audience?
A.5.12.gaps: Classification is assigned mechanically without owner judgment.
review: Sample data sets and compare classifications with impact and handling needs.
Consult information owners and the classification scheme owner. Who decides classification when information changes purpose or audience?
evidence_examples: Classification scheme, data inventory and owner decisions.
Owner decisions in a data inventory linking protection needs to classification.
outcome: Information classifications reflect owner judgment and protection needs.

A.5.13.title: Classification labels
A.5.13.author: Omnisciente
A.5.13.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.13.plain: Make information classifications recognizable where labels help people or systems handle data appropriately.
A.5.13.start: Inspect representative labels across documents, email and applicable systems.
A.5.13.evidence: Labelling guidance, labelled samples and applicable tool settings.
A.5.13.ask: Consult information owners and people applying or consuming labels. How do labels help recipients choose the right handling action?
A.5.13.gaps: Labels conflict with the classification scheme or lack handling instructions.
review: Inspect representative labels across documents, email and applicable systems.
Consult information owners and people applying or consuming labels. How do labels help recipients choose the right handling action?
evidence_examples: Labelling guidance, labelled samples and applicable tool settings.
Representative labels and handling instructions suited to the information format.
outcome: Labels communicate classifications and actionable handling expectations.

A.5.14.title: Protected information transfers
A.5.14.author: Omnisciente
A.5.14.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.14.plain: Protect information when it is transferred between people, systems or organizations.
A.5.14.start: Sample an external information transfer and its approved protection method.
A.5.14.evidence: Transfer procedures, agreement terms and relevant channel configurations.
A.5.14.ask: Consult information owners and people authorizing or operating transfers. What checks occur before sensitive information leaves the organization?
A.5.14.gaps: Transfers use unapproved channels or recipient checks are absent.
review: Sample an external information transfer and its approved protection method.
Consult information owners and people authorizing or operating transfers. What checks occur before sensitive information leaves the organization?
evidence_examples: Transfer procedures, agreement terms and relevant channel configurations.
An approved transfer record with recipient verification and channel protection evidence.
outcome: Transfers protect information through approved channels and recipient checks.

A.5.15.title: Access rules
A.5.15.author: Omnisciente
A.5.15.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.15.plain: Establish access rules that connect business need to appropriate information and system permissions.
A.5.15.start: Compare a role's permitted access with documented business need and rules.
A.5.15.evidence: Access policy, role definitions and approval criteria.
A.5.15.ask: Consult information or system owners and access approvers. What rule determines whether an access request should be approved?
A.5.15.gaps: Access rules are broad permissions without a business justification.
review: Compare a role's permitted access with documented business need and rules.
Consult information or system owners and access approvers. What rule determines whether an access request should be approved?
evidence_examples: Access policy, role definitions and approval criteria.
Role design and access-decision records applying business-need criteria.
outcome: Access rules tie permissions to documented business need.

A.5.16.title: Identity lifecycle
A.5.16.author: Omnisciente
A.5.16.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.16.plain: Manage identities through creation, change and retirement rather than only at initial provisioning.
A.5.16.start: Trace a joiner, role transfer and leaver through identity records.
A.5.16.evidence: Identity records, provisioning/change tickets and deactivation evidence.
A.5.16.ask: Consult identity lifecycle owners and people initiating joiner, mover or leaver changes. How are orphaned, duplicate and non-human identities detected?
A.5.16.gaps: Identity retirement omits relevant non-human or shared identities where these are used.
review: Trace a joiner, role transfer and leaver through identity records.
Consult identity lifecycle owners and people initiating joiner, mover or leaver changes. How are orphaned, duplicate and non-human identities detected?
evidence_examples: Identity records, provisioning/change tickets and deactivation evidence.
Provisioning, transfer and retirement records reconciled with active identities.
outcome: Identity creation, changes and retirement cover relevant identity types.

A.5.17.title: Credential handling
A.5.17.author: Omnisciente
A.5.17.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.17.plain: Handle authentication information so credentials are issued, protected and changed appropriately.
A.5.17.start: Inspect credential issuance and reset processes without collecting secret values.
A.5.17.evidence: Credential-handling procedures and configuration evidence without credential values.
A.5.17.ask: Consult authentication process owners and people handling credential issuance or resets. How is the recipient verified before authentication information is issued?
A.5.17.gaps: Credentials are exposed in tickets or reset identity checks are weak.
review: Inspect credential issuance and reset processes without collecting secret values.
Consult authentication process owners and people handling credential issuance or resets. How is the recipient verified before authentication information is issued?
evidence_examples: Credential-handling procedures and configuration evidence without credential values.
Observed credential issuance or reset workflow with verified recipients and no secret values.
outcome: Credential issuance and resets protect secrets and verify recipients.

A.5.18.title: Access entitlement lifecycle
A.5.18.author: Omnisciente
A.5.18.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.18.plain: Approve, review, change and remove access rights as people's responsibilities and needs change.
A.5.18.start: Sample access approvals, periodic reviews and revocations after role changes.
A.5.18.evidence: Access approvals, review records and revocation tickets.
A.5.18.ask: Consult access approvers, entitlement reviewers and affected system owners. How does a reviewer know which entitlements are still needed?
A.5.18.gaps: Reviews approve account lists without examining actual privileges.
review: Sample access approvals, periodic reviews and revocations after role changes.
Consult access approvers, entitlement reviewers and affected system owners. How does a reviewer know which entitlements are still needed?
evidence_examples: Access approvals, review records and revocation tickets.
Entitlement-level review decisions and removal records linked to changed responsibilities.
outcome: Access rights change with need and are meaningfully reviewed.

A.5.19.title: Supplier security
A.5.19.author: Omnisciente
A.5.19.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.19.plain: Manage the security exposure introduced by supplier relationships.
A.5.19.start: Sample a supplier's security risk assessment and assigned relationship owner.
A.5.19.evidence: Supplier inventory, risk assessments and accountable business owners.
A.5.19.ask: Consult supplier relationship owners and security risk assessors. What triggers deeper assurance for a high-risk supplier?
A.5.19.gaps: Supplier selection omits the information or access exposure it introduces.
review: Sample a supplier's security risk assessment and assigned relationship owner.
Consult supplier relationship owners and security risk assessors. What triggers deeper assurance for a high-risk supplier?
evidence_examples: Supplier inventory, risk assessments and accountable business owners.
Supplier assessments linked to actual data or access exposure and relationship ownership.
outcome: Supplier security exposure is evaluated with accountable ownership.

A.5.20.title: Contractual supplier safeguards
A.5.20.author: Omnisciente
A.5.20.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.20.plain: Include appropriate security expectations in supplier agreements.
A.5.20.start: Compare a supplier agreement with its assessed security requirements.
A.5.20.evidence: Security clauses, negotiated requirements and approved agreement records.
A.5.20.ask: Consult contract owners and people reviewing supplier security terms. Which agreement terms support breach reporting and secure termination?
A.5.20.gaps: Important security expectations remain verbal or absent from the agreement.
review: Compare a supplier agreement with its assessed security requirements.
Consult contract owners and people reviewing supplier security terms. Which agreement terms support breach reporting and secure termination?
evidence_examples: Security clauses, negotiated requirements and approved agreement records.
An approved agreement or security addendum covering the relevant supplier expectations.
outcome: Supplier agreements capture appropriate security commitments.

A.5.21.title: Technology supply-chain safeguards
A.5.21.author: Omnisciente
A.5.21.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.21.plain: Consider security risks across the technology supply chain, not just the direct supplier.
A.5.21.start: Trace a technology service through key components and upstream dependencies.
A.5.21.evidence: Technology supplier assessments, dependency records and supply-chain risk decisions.
A.5.21.ask: Consult technology procurement owners and people assessing critical dependencies. How are material supply-chain changes and component risks evaluated? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
A.5.21.gaps: Assessment stops at the direct vendor and ignores critical dependencies.
review: Trace a technology service through key components and upstream dependencies.

Consult technology procurement owners and people assessing critical dependencies. How are material supply-chain changes and component risks evaluated? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
evidence_examples: Technology supplier assessments, dependency records and supply-chain risk decisions.
Component or dependency assessments with evaluated upstream technology risks.
outcome: Technology supply-chain decisions consider critical upstream dependencies.

A.5.22.title: Supplier service oversight
A.5.22.author: Omnisciente
A.5.22.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.22.plain: Review supplier service performance and manage changes that affect security.
A.5.22.start: Inspect a supplier service review and a material service change.
A.5.22.evidence: Service reviews, assurance follow-up and change records.
A.5.22.ask: Consult supplier service owners and assurance reviewers. How are adverse assurance results tracked to resolution? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
A.5.22.gaps: Assurance reports are filed without findings or service-change follow-up.
review: Inspect a supplier service review and a material service change.

Consult supplier service owners and assurance reviewers. How are adverse assurance results tracked to resolution? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
evidence_examples: Service reviews, assurance follow-up and change records.
Service-review decisions and tracked assurance or security-change follow-up.
outcome: Supplier changes and adverse assurance results receive tracked follow-up.

A.5.23.title: Cloud service governance
A.5.23.author: Omnisciente
A.5.23.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.23.plain: Manage cloud use deliberately through acquisition, operation and exit, including shared responsibilities.
A.5.23.start: Inspect a cloud service's acquisition, shared responsibilities and exit arrangements.
A.5.23.evidence: Cloud inventory, responsibility model, configuration reviews and exit arrangements.
A.5.23.ask: Consult cloud service owners and the people assigned customer-side security responsibilities. Who controls configuration and recovery when the provider manages the platform? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
A.5.23.gaps: Cloud use has no responsibility boundary or workable exit plan.
review: Inspect a cloud service's acquisition, shared responsibilities and exit arrangements.

Consult cloud service owners and the people assigned customer-side security responsibilities. Who controls configuration and recovery when the provider manages the platform? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
evidence_examples: Cloud inventory, responsibility model, configuration reviews and exit arrangements.
Cloud acquisition and exit decisions with documented shared responsibilities.
outcome: Cloud acquisition, operation and exit have understood responsibilities.

A.5.24.title: Incident preparation
A.5.24.author: Omnisciente
A.5.24.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.24.plain: Prepare the roles, procedures and resources needed to handle security incidents.
A.5.24.start: Walk incident preparation through relevant roles, escalation, communications and resources, using a readiness check, exercise or actual response record.
A.5.24.evidence: Incident plan, responsibilities, contact routes and exercise records.
A.5.24.ask: Consult incident coordinators and designated responders. Can responders obtain the plan and contacts when normal systems are unavailable?
A.5.24.gaps: Response readiness is unverified or escalation responsibilities conflict.
review: Walk incident preparation through relevant roles, escalation, communications and resources, using a readiness check, exercise or actual response record.
Consult incident coordinators and designated responders. Can responders obtain the plan and contacts when normal systems are unavailable?
evidence_examples: Incident plan, responsibilities, contact routes and exercise records.
Exercise records showing usable incident roles, communication and escalation.
outcome: Incident response roles and procedures are usable in an exercised scenario.

A.5.25.title: Event triage
A.5.25.author: Omnisciente
A.5.25.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.25.plain: Assess security events and decide which require incident response.
A.5.25.start: Sample a security event from initial report to documented incident classification.
A.5.25.evidence: Triage criteria, event records and escalation decisions.
A.5.25.ask: Consult event triage owners and escalation decision makers. Which criteria distinguish an event from an incident requiring response?
A.5.25.gaps: Classification depends on personal judgment without escalation criteria.
review: Sample a security event from initial report to documented incident classification.
Consult event triage owners and escalation decision makers. Which criteria distinguish an event from an incident requiring response?
evidence_examples: Triage criteria, event records and escalation decisions.
Event triage records demonstrating classification and escalation decisions.
outcome: Event classification applies defined criteria and escalation routes.

A.5.26.title: Incident response execution
A.5.26.author: Omnisciente
A.5.26.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.26.plain: Carry out a coordinated response when a security incident is identified.
A.5.26.start: Trace a confirmed incident through containment, communications and recovery.
A.5.26.evidence: Response procedures, incident timelines and recorded actions.
A.5.26.ask: Consult incident responders and people authorizing consequential response decisions. Who authorized consequential response actions and recorded the timeline?
A.5.26.gaps: Response actions lack coordination or an accountable decision trail.
review: Trace a confirmed incident through containment, communications and recovery.
Consult incident responders and people authorizing consequential response decisions. Who authorized consequential response actions and recorded the timeline?
evidence_examples: Response procedures, incident timelines and recorded actions.
A retained incident timeline identifying authorized response and recovery decisions.
outcome: Incident response has a coordinated timeline and accountable decisions.

A.5.27.title: Incident lessons
A.5.27.author: Omnisciente
A.5.27.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.27.plain: Use incident experience to improve the security program.
A.5.27.start: Follow one incident lesson into an improvement and validation.
A.5.27.evidence: Lessons-learned records, assigned improvements and follow-up validation.
A.5.27.ask: Consult incident review facilitators and assigned improvement owners. What changed because of the incident and how was that change checked?
A.5.27.gaps: Lessons are documented but never assigned or evaluated.
review: Follow one incident lesson into an improvement and validation.
Consult incident review facilitators and assigned improvement owners. What changed because of the incident and how was that change checked?
evidence_examples: Lessons-learned records, assigned improvements and follow-up validation.
An improvement record linked to an incident lesson and follow-up evaluation.
outcome: Incident lessons result in improvements with validation.

A.5.28.title: Incident evidence preservation
A.5.28.author: Omnisciente
A.5.28.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.28.plain: Preserve incident-related evidence in a way that supports its intended use and traceability.
A.5.28.start: Inspect the collection, preservation and access history of an incident artifact or an evidence-handling exercise.
A.5.28.evidence: Evidence-handling procedure, collection records and provenance.

A.5.28.gaps: Artifacts have no provenance or handling compromises their intended use.
review: Inspect the collection, preservation and access history of an incident artifact or an evidence-handling exercise.
Consult evidence custodians and relevant legal or investigation advisers. How would you demonstrate an artifact's origin and handling history?
evidence_examples: Evidence-handling procedure, collection records and provenance.
Collection and handling records preserving artifact origin, integrity and access history.
outcome: Incident artifacts retain provenance and appropriate handling protection.

A.5.29.title: Security during disruptions
A.5.29.author: Omnisciente
A.5.29.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.29.plain: Maintain appropriate information security while operating under disruptive conditions.
A.5.29.start: Inspect disruption arrangements or exercise results for appropriate emergency access and information handling.

A.5.29.gaps: Emergency processes bypass security without bounded approval or follow-up.
review: Inspect disruption arrangements or exercise results for appropriate emergency access and information handling.
Consult continuity owners and security owners for degraded operations. Which security safeguards must remain effective during degraded operations?
evidence_examples: Continuity procedures, emergency access decisions and exercise results.
Disruption exercise observations showing emergency access and information-handling safeguards.
outcome: Security remains appropriately controlled during degraded operations.

A.5.30.title: ICT continuity preparedness
A.5.30.author: Omnisciente
A.5.30.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.30.plain: Prepare technology to support the organization's continuity needs.
A.5.30.start: Compare recovery capabilities and test results with business continuity needs.
A.5.30.evidence: Recovery requirements, plans, dependency information and test results.
A.5.30.ask: Consult technology recovery owners and business continuity decision makers. Which critical dependency limits the achievable recovery time? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
A.5.30.gaps: Recovery plans exist but technology cannot meet business needs in testing.
review: Compare recovery capabilities and test results with business continuity needs.

Consult technology recovery owners and business continuity decision makers. Which critical dependency limits the achievable recovery time? If the assessed activity is outsourced, include the provider responsible for that activity.
evidence_examples: Recovery requirements, plans, dependency information and test results.
Recovery-test results compared with continuity needs and critical dependencies.
outcome: Technology recovery capability supports evaluated continuity needs.

A.5.31.title: Applicable obligations
A.5.31.author: Omnisciente
A.5.31.content_label: Omnisciente-authored implementation guidance — not official ISO text
A.5.31.plain: Identify and manage the obligations relevant to information security within the ISMS scope.
